REFILL WITH A LITTLE ROOM TO WANDER

Your journey, your order.

Start somewhere familiar. Add only the stops you want. Keep each stop when you move to Google Maps.

Demonstration refills remain fictional. External directions need connectivity and do not establish water availability, opening hours or path accessibility.

1. Choose your start

Ordering is a suggestion, not road routing or a shortest-path guarantee. No step-free or shaded route is promised.

2. Review your stops

    3. Take it with you

    For mobile compatibility, long journeys split into parts of at most three intermediate stops. Each part begins where the previous part ends. Individual-leg links are also provided.

    A HELLO CAN BE A GOOD BEGINNING

    A refill. A welcome.
    No purchase required.

    The idea: independent bookshops, antique stores and other willing local businesses can offer a friendly refill. Participation would be voluntary, and buying something would always be optional.

    01

    Ask the owner

    Agree on water suitability, how bottles are filled, hours, step access and a no-purchase refill policy. Low footfall does not imply permission or capacity.

    02

    Make it clear

    Display an opt-in sticker and a short bilingual phrase. Show the last check, known limits and how a shop can pause or leave.

    Olá! Participam no programa de enchimento gratuito de garrafas?

    03

    Keep it voluntary

    No obligation to chat, spend money or share a location history. A welcoming public refill remains an alternative.

    Record a suggestion

    This prototype saves a draft on this device. It does not submit to an operator, contact a business or add a verified point.

    ALUNUÉ · STUDENT LIFE IN ÉVORA

    Trust before the next tap.

    A focused HCI proposal for discovering refills during the student day, with optional groceries, local encounters and cultural stops.

    Tonight: research

    Phase 1 needs the research report: real UÉ evidence, three personas, empathy/journey maps, main tasks, usability requirements and HTA. This prototype supports discussion; it does not replace research.

    Next: evaluate

    Paper tasks, medium-fidelity design, cross-group heuristic review, then high-fidelity testing with at least five real UÉ users and SUS, following the course brief.

    Later: expand

    Confirmed refill inventory, willing shops, route-provider integration and accessibility surveys. Android installation before deciding whether a signed APK adds value.

    Evidence and limits

    Informal feedback is reported from memory. Original notes are unavailable; exact counts, questions and participant eligibility have not been reconstructed. Proposed personas are hypotheses. No real refill partner or working public refill has been verified here.

    Privacy & offline behaviour

    No account or analytics in the application. Optional location stays in session memory; opening directions sends chosen coordinates to Google. Map, weather and sight requests use a fixed Évora area and expose the request to those providers. Private hosting has its own access gate. Saved journeys, local drafts and API snapshots remain on this browser. Clear them here or in browser settings.

    First online visit is needed to cache the app shell. Offline use depends on browser support and retained storage. No offline street map or turn-by-turn navigation is included.
